summary:
STAFFORD TOWN'S DEMOLITION JOB

Stafford Town produced an absolutely clinical performance away at New Mills on Tuesday night, winning 5-0 in a display that suggests they could be serious contenders this season. They were already 4-0 up at half-time, with Dan Jones, Pat Mazurkiewicz, Eshan Greer and another quick strike doing the damage. New Mills, who had looked impressive in their opening 6-0 rout of Telford, completely fell apart defensively. Stafford added a fifth through Dan Clarkson in the second half. It's a stark reminder that opening day performances can be misleading — Stafford's manager has clearly got them organised and they're clearly not a team to take lightly in midweek fixtures.

ECCLESHALL'S PERFECT START CONTINUES

Eccleshall made it two wins from two with a comprehensive 4-0 victory at Allscott Heath on Wednesday evening. Will Silvester, Nicky Parker and Essa Faburay were among the scorers in what appears to have been a dominant performance. They've also made a smart signing in Phil McKerdy from Wolverhampton Casuals ahead of the Allscott fixture, bolstering their defence. At this rate they could challenge for the title.

WOLVERHAMPTON CASUALS LOOKING SOLID

The Casuals' opening day 3-0 win at Crewe now looks even more impressive given how competitive the new boys from Crewe have shown themselves to be. Three different goalscorers suggests they've got options across the pitch, and they're now preparing for their first home league game against Market Drayton on Wednesday.

FOLEY MEIR'S DRAMATIC HOME BOW

Foley Meir played out an absolute thriller at home to Sandbach on Sunday evening, eventually losing 3-2 despite leading 3-1. It was a game with everything — Sandbach took the lead early, Jake Lovatt equalized on his home debut with a volley from a free-kick, then Foley went 2-1 up before taking a 3-1 lead through Lucas Baker's 25-yard strike. But Sandbach showed character to pull one back late on, leaving Foley frustrated after what looked like a match-winning position. Monty pulled off a fantastic save late on to deny them an equalizer.

SANDBACH'S RESILIENCE

Sandbach deserve credit for their comeback against Foley Meir even though they ultimately came up short. They went from 3-1 down to nearly salvaging a point, and their opening day win at Wednesfield Community showed they can be resilient competitors. Joe Bevvy has also just been confirmed as Sandbach's highest-ever scorer with 54 goals — he's only been there two seasons.

CREWE'S TOUGH START

Newly promoted Crewe have lost both their opening fixtures, going down 3-0 at home to Wolverhampton Casuals and then 1-1 at Telford on Tuesday in what looks like a difficult baptism into the NWCFL. They've been active in the transfer market with a new Brazilian centre-back in Juliano Silva arriving, but the results suggest they might struggle this season.
